slice: engine + CLI: sc-jev-check (config, extract, payload, run, session, registry, equal_input) and sc-ai

findings.issue: Equal-input attestation is hard-wired to always say true: every JudgeRequest.payload is bundle.clone() of the same bundle (409-411) so same_bytes is always true; leak = outcomes.len() != backends.len() is always false because any judge error returns early via judged? (309). Tests only confirm the constant. ADR-SAG-0019 says the record 'records whether every backend saw the same canonical bytes'; code never compares wire bytes.
findings.recommendation: (a) Make it honest: backends report a digest of canonical bytes they put on the wire, compare those. (b) Drop same_bytes and payloads Vec, set equal:true/leak:false directly and document that it attests construction, not observation. Either way delete dead payloads accumulation.

findings.issue: Second and later LLM backends receive earlier backends' answers in their system prompt (render_session_context(prior) at 400-405; tests assert Haiku's prompt contains Jev's choice), yet the run reports equal:true. Anchors the second judge; works against the 'compare answers to Jev' equal-input goal in intent.md:10-14. Mandated by ADR-SAG-0008.
options: Independent by default: no prior answers in run_request; session context only in ask. Cheapest, matches equal-input claim, amend ADR-SAG-0008.
Explicit RunOptions::chain_context(bool)/mode enum recorded on EqualInputRecord as context: independent|chained. Keeps both; attestation truthful.
Keep chaining but hash full per-backend wire input and record next to prompt_sha256. Most honest, bigger types change.

findings.issue: Four overlapping public entry points accumulated across a-3/a-6/a-7: build_request(repo,rev,check_path) loads the file; run_check(&CheckSpec) requires caller to load_check_at first (sc-ai command.rs:439, sc-jev-py run.rs:72); run_request(&RunRequest); prepare_caller_request(bytes) returns PreparedCallerRequest = RunRequest + backends - producer so sc-ai rebuilds a RunRequest (484-488). Two prompt loaders duplicate each other (prompt.rs:13-66); needs_llm/require_backends computed twice; backend defaulting to Jev decided in three places (mod.rs:368-374, command.rs:440-444, py run.rs:566). sc-jev-py exposes no caller-request path.
options: Source enum CheckSource {File{path}, Spec(CheckSpec), CallerJson(bytes)} with prepare(&CheckSource,&PrepareOptions)->RunRequest and run(RunRequest,RunOptions)->CheckResult; keep build_request/run_check as deprecated shims. One path, M effort.
run_check takes a path like build_request; prepare_caller_request returns RunRequest with backends field. Lower churn, duplication partly stays.
Builder CheckRun::from_check(path)/from_request(bytes).backends().prompt_override().dry_run().execute(). Most ergonomic for MCP, most new surface.

findings.issue: a-6 session layer costs more than it delivers: FileSessionStore holds Arc<RwLock<BackendRegistry>>; install_registry is a temporal-coupling step run_request performs (run/mod.rs:270) and sc-ai must repeat before ask (command.rs:535-539); sc-ai loads the session twice; SessionStore trait (create, ask only) is not what the engine uses (RunOptions.sessions is concrete; inherent open/load/record_outcome); SessionStore::create used only in tests; run_request writes a session file with the whole payload even for Jev-only runs where ask is refused; each backend iteration reloads the session from disk when outcomes is in memory; session_log injected twice.
options: Stateless store: FileSessionStore{dir,ttl,clock} with save/load/ask(id,text,&BackendRegistry,&SharedSessionLog); delete install_registry, RwLock and the trait until a second store exists. Smallest and most honest. M.
Keep a real trait: save/load/append, RunOptions.sessions: Arc<dyn SessionStore>, ask as free engine fn. Enables in-memory store for MCP/tests.
Keep current shape, document install_registry. Zero effort; Phase B inherits hidden ordering requirement.

findings.issue: ADR-SAG-0009 promises a new backend 'registers without caller changes'; in practice requires edits across three crates + types: BackendId closed 3-variant enum, no FromStr, no capability methods (ids.rs:134-151); backend_key_id (104-110), construct_backend (142-157), is_llm twice (session/mod.rs:437, scripted.rs:88), parse_backend three times, the 'jev, anthropic_haiku, or openai_luna' string in four messages + help, ask capability inferred from is_llm, packaged-config vendor check requires exactly typesafe/anthropic/openai (config/mod.rs:185-191).
options: JudgeBackend::capabilities() -> {needs_system_prompt, supports_ask}; FromStr and key_id() on BackendId; #[non_exhaustive]; one construct_backend match; engine reads capabilities never ids. S-M, cross-crate.

Single static BACKENDS: &[BackendSpec{id,name,aliases,key,llm,construct}] table in sc-jev-check iterated by every parser/help/registry builder. Keeps enum closed; edits limited to one table + one arm.
String/newtype BackendId(Cow<'static,str>) with runtime registry. Truly open for local judges; loses exhaustiveness; serde change on every record.

findings.issue: Documented {path} placeholder for command inputs cannot be used from check.toml: production dispatch always passes source_path None (extract/mod.rs:76); substitute_placeholders rejects {path} without a source (command.rs:113-117); InputSpec::Command has no path field; no non-test caller passes Some. Yet docs/sc-jev-check/extraction.md:32 shows the sc-treesitter example using {path}. Fails with CONFIG_INVALID.
options: Add path: Option<String> to InputSpec::Command (types change), validate with validate_relative, substitute. Makes the documented example work.
Remove {path} from placeholders and docs; delete source_path parameter. Users write the literal path. Simplest.
First-class kind=treesitter input building argv itself. Most ergonomic; reintroduces producer knowledge the facade (ADR-SAG-0015) avoids.

findings.issue: Sealed Extractor trait is decorative: extract_input matches InputSpec and calls free functions (71-78); Extractor::extract returns Vec<Subject>, dropping Extracted.document which equal-input needs; extractor_for used by one test; each free function begins with an impossible 'wrong input kind' branch. Mandated by RBP-F004 note in architecture.md:351-353.
options: Enum dispatch only: delete trait, private::Sealed, extractor_for, four unit structs; extractors take destructured fields. ~80 lines removed; amend RBP-F004 note.
Keep sealed trait as the real dispatch path returning Extracted. More ceremony, no new capability.

findings.issue: Production system prompt ships a test sentinel PACKAGED-PROMPT-TOKEN-a3, compiled into binary and wheel and sent to Anthropic/OpenAI on every LLM judge call. Asserted by config/mod.rs:263, exact.rs:399, run/mod.rs:597.
findings.recommendation: Remove token from asset; tests check PACKAGED_SYSTEM_PROMPT == include_str!(asset) and use a prompt override file for sentinel checks.

findings.issue: Packaged jev.toml config nothing uses: vendor model pins validated but never read (asset comment says 'HTTP clients in later sprints read these ids'; none do); system_prompt_file decorative (PackagedAsset branch ignores resolved.path, prompt.rs:48-51); compile-time asset re-parsed 3-4 times per run (payload/mod.rs:65,90; prompt.rs:45; caller.rs:49); BuiltPayload.prompt computed then ignored; resolve_prompt_path needless lifetimes.
findings.recommendation: Replace jev.toml with documented consts or parse once into OnceLock; delete vendors/VendorPin and BuiltPayload.prompt; asset-validity check as unit test.

findings.issue: Same helpers implemented 2-3x across engine, sc-ai, sc-jev-py and already diverge: backend parsing (engine+sc-ai serde INPUT_INVALID; py match with hyphen aliases returning CONFIG_INVALID); state validation twice with different rules (parse_state rejects repeated question ids, caller validate_state does not; caller JSON skips empty-id/empty-instructions checks); is_llm x2 (+test copy); utf8_payload x2; Rev parsing x2 (py treats empty as WORKTREE, sc-ai does not).
findings.recommendation: impl FromStr for BackendId + BackendId::is_llm() (or capabilities), Rev::parse; one validate_question_set and one validate_state in payload/questions.rs used by both paths; sc-ai and sc-jev-py call engine helpers only.

findings.issue: Response contract defined only inside the CLI: run_data/merge_jev_response (566-646) decide which outcome becomes top-level answers (outcomes.first(), so --backend anthropic_haiku --backend jev puts Haiku on top) and which provider_meta keys survive; envelope() pub(crate); sc-jev-py exposes raw outcomes/equal_input/payload with no normalised answers; error envelope has no version while success has version:1; exit codes 0/2 inline in main.rs.
options: sc_jev_check::response::RunResponse {answers, model, usage, session_id, prompt_sha256, outcomes, equal_input, payload?} built from CheckResult; sc-ai wraps in envelope, py converts to dict, MCP returns as tool result. ADR-SAG-0014 becomes an engine contract.
Envelope + response types in sc-agent-types next to ScAgentErrorResponse (add version to error body). Centralises wire contract in types crate.
Keep CLI-only shaping, document sc-jev-py as raw surface. MCP re-implements merge_jev_response.

findings.issue: Correctness-affecting policy re-implemented per composition root: repo-root discovery is git toplevel in sc-ai (709-737) vs raw current_dir() in sc-jev-py (run.rs:154-164); since repo root is the base for .env key resolution (ADR-SAG-0003), the same check resolves keys differently from a subdirectory. sc-observability adapter copied nearly line for line with divergent error construction (operational_config vs session_store_io), flush semantics, and fallback action name. ADR-SAG-0021 path precedence differs by design, so a Python-created session cannot be asked from the CLI without flags.
options: Engine owns discover_repo_root(Option<&Path>) (git toplevel, fallback explicit); accept duplicated obs adapter until v2 shim removal (bead agt-obs-v2-shim-removal). S effort, fixes correctness.
Also move adapter into sc-agent-types behind observability-adapter feature pulling full sc-observability. Widens types crate deps against ADR-SAG-0016.
Small unpublished sc-agent-compose crate shared by sc-ai, sc-jev-py, future MCP holding repo discovery, path precedence, adapter. Cleanest for Phase B; amends ADR-SAG-0016 'no extra crate'.

findings.issue: If any backend after the first fails, run returns only the error; answers already obtained (and paid for) never reach the caller though persisted to the session file; caller gets a JevError with no session_id. The leak field was apparently meant for this and is unreachable (ARCHE-001).
options: Per-backend results: CheckResult.outcomes: Vec<BackendResult{backend, result: Result<JudgeOutcome,JevError>}>, leak = any failed; CLI exits non-zero but prints envelope. Most useful for comparison; breaking CheckResult change. M.
Fail fast with progress: RunFailure{error, session_id, partial}. Smaller; second error type at engine boundary.
Keep fail-fast and document; leak stays meaningless.

findings.issue: validate_for_send runs up to 3x per backend; pre-loop validates with prior=&[] (271-276), loop validates with real prior (298), backends validate inside judge. Pre-flight prompt has no session context so a token-budget check can pass pre-flight and fail mid-run after earlier backends were charged.
findings.recommendation: Keep pre-flight (ADR-SAG-0004 refuse-before-send); drop the in-loop call or keep only for context-bearing request; if chaining stays, pre-flight should allow worst-case context size.

findings.issue: Producer stderr captured into a 4 KiB sink then dropped (161-165, 316-328); ExtractionFailed carries only exit code so an sc-treesitter failure is undiagnosable; read_git_show maps every non-zero exit to InputMissing{path} (read.rs:87-93). Impossible child.stdout/stderr None branches (142-159) could be expect.
findings.recommendation: Sanitized stderr tail in ExtractionFailed.detail; distinguish 'path not in rev' from invalid rev / other git failure; expect on impossible branches.

findings.issue: Sprint scaffolding in shipped layout: [[test]] a6_exact at src/run/exact.rs re-implements TempDir/Capture/JsonlSink/QUESTIONS/bare_repo and repeats tests already in session/mod.rs and run/mod.rs; lib.rs:3-4 'Sprint a-1 freezes this mod list' blocks refactors; five separate JudgeBackend test doubles (run/mod.rs:440, exact.rs:72, registry/mod.rs:165, session/mod.rs:555, sc-ai tests/cli.rs:43) next to test_util::MockJudgeBackend/ScriptedJudge. run/mod.rs 1050 lines but ~635 tests.
findings.recommendation: Move exact.rs to tests/ or delete duplicates; drop freeze comment; one capture double in sc_agent_types::test_util.

findings.issue: Public surface far wider than sc-ai/sc-jev-py use: PayloadBuilder, refuse_over_cap, parse_state, STATE_SCHEMA, four extractor structs, read_repo_bytes/text, parse_subjects_bytes, validate_subjects_document, equal_input::{record,commands_for,same_bytes,producer_from_extractions}, render_session_context, FileSessionStore::load_raw, registry::backend_key_id. External consumers use only config::{load_check_at,CheckSpec,PACKAGED_SYSTEM_PROMPT}, run::*, session::{FileSessionStore,SessionStore}, registry::{BackendRegistry,registry_for_repo,register_scripted_backends}. prepare_caller_request lives in run but wraps payload/caller. sc-ai lib.rs re-exports observe items and ungated ExecuteOverrides while boundary facade is sc_ai::execute. equal_input is a top-level module for four small fns.
findings.recommendation: pub(crate) these; fold equal_input into run; move caller-request prep into payload; update jev-check.toml facade.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled ~200-line argv parser with real bugs: --help/-h anywhere short-circuits (so `ask --text --help` prints help); next_value/assign reject values starting with '-' (`--text "-1 is wrong"`, `--rev -` fail); every flag listed in three places + reject lists + static help.
options: clap derive (Subcommand run/dry-run/ask, conflicts_with). ~250 lines removed, edge cases fixed; one dependency.
Keep custom: fix --help check to args[0..2], allow --flag=-value, table-drive flags. No dependency, S.

findings.issue: Dry-run writes to disk: creates <repo>/.sc-ai/, starts a logger writer thread, creates sessions dir because RunOptions requires FileSessionStore and logger even when nothing is sent. Same in sc-jev-py and cross_impl_branches.rs:98.
findings.recommendation: RunOptions.sessions Option (required only when !dry_run) or split dry_run(request)->CheckResult needing neither.

findings.issue: table-column subjects carry a span covering the whole row while text is only the cell (110-111), breaking the invariant subjects.rs:121-126 enforces (text.len() == end-start). producer_from_extractions keeps only the first document (equal_input/mod.rs:66-75) so a check with two producers attests to one.
findings.recommendation: Compute cell byte span in split_row; make EqualInputRecord.producer a list or reject multiple producers explicitly.

findings.issue: Library extractor reads process stdin when path is '-' ignoring rev (48-55); hidden side effect for embedders (Python interpreter stdin, MCP stdio transport would lose protocol bytes).
findings.recommendation: Drop '-' from check.toml inputs or have the composition root supply stdin bytes explicitly as sc-ai does for --request-json -.

findings.issue: Non-config failures labelled ConfigInvalid with string-prefixed sub-kinds: clock before epoch -> ConfigInvalid (465); registry misses registry_invalid (registry/mod.rs:79); session dir session_store_io; corrupt session file session_document_invalid (INPUT_INVALID); distinguished only by 'registry: '/'session-store: '/'operational: ' prefixes in detail. Consumers parse strings.
options: Real variants SessionStoreIo/RegistryInvalid/Operational keeping existing code() strings.
Keep variants, add JevError::category() derived from prefix. Less churn, still stringly inside.

findings.issue: --check resolution canonicalizes against the worktree even with --rev (745), so a check file existing only at that revision fails INPUT_MISSING though load_check_at would read via git show; --rev silently accepted and ignored with --request-json; prompt path joined twice (sc-ai 416-419 and prompt.rs:79-83).
findings.recommendation: Normalise --check lexically; let engine validate_relative/git show decide existence; reject --rev with --request-json; pass raw prompt path.

findings.issue: Worktree reads follow symlinks out of the repo: validate_relative is lexical (38-60); read_worktree does fs::read(repo.join(relative)) without canonicalize + prefix check (62-73). A committed symlink can pull arbitrary local files into a payload sent to third-party LLMs. (git-rev path safe.)
findings.recommendation: Canonicalize and assert prefix before reading, or refuse symlinks.

solid: Command extractor process handling production grade: argv no shell, cwd repo root, stdin null, stdout 8 MiB cap, polling timeout, bounded kill/reap
Session files atomic 0600 temp+fsync+rename; TTL from created_at; injectable clock; capped reads; digest re-verified on load
Prompt/payload separation (ADR-SAG-0019) enforced in one place (encode_payload); inline system_prompt in caller JSON rejected without echo; override does not change prompt_sha256
Repo-relative validation + git show --end-of-options closes absolute/../drive/option-injection on the rev path
ADR-SAG-0022 scripted backends do not leak into production builds (cfg(any(test, feature)), resolver-2 dev-dep isolation verified)
Dry-run never resolves keys or constructs HTTP backends; registry Debug prints ids only
deny_unknown_fields throughout config and payload parsing; caller-JSON errors do not echo the document
sc-ai keeps thin-adapter boundary: no HTTP deps, stdout one envelope, stderr one typed JSON error
verdict: Mostly solid work but not ready for Phase B to build on without fixes. Low-level pieces are careful. Problems are in the layers above, grown sprint by sprint: four engine entry points where one would do; session store carrying mutable registry state callers must install before ask; decorative extractor trait; two hollow guarantees (equal-input record can only say equal:true/leak:false; documented {path} placeholder unusable). sc-ai and sc-jev-py each re-implement backend parsing, repo discovery and the logging adapter with divergent behaviour (different error codes; different repo-root and therefore .env resolution). Response contract lives only in the CLI. Routine items clearable in a day or two. Owner decisions needed: ARCHE-002 (independent vs chained multi-backend; contradicts equal-input claim), ARCHE-013 (mid-run failure semantics), ARCHE-003/004 (single entry point, session redesign), ARCHE-005 (how open the backend set is), ARCHE-011 (where the response/envelope contract lives), ARCHE-012 (where composition-root policy is shared). ARCHE-002, -003, -005, -011 hurt most once Phase B adds agents, producers and an MCP consumer.
